project.title: Digitalian Folktales
project.description: A digital edition of Calvino's Fiabe Italiane, with regional language comparison.
project.introText: Digitalian Folktales is a digital edition of tales from Italo Calvino's Fiabe italiane, read alongside the regional versions Calvino drew on.

gridImages.caption: Parallel reading: the Friulian field record beside its Italian translation, aligned passage by passage so each can be cited, with a map of related tales and the tale's record card.
Comparing stories: the Friulian and Sicilian cycles as catalogue cards, showing the tale type (ATU 774) they share.
Search in use: 'lepre' (hare) finds episode II of the Friulian cycle, La coratella di lepre.

project.middleText: The comparison view sets two versions of the same tale side by side, such as Gesù e San Pietro in Friuli and in Sicilia, each with its original dialect text and an Italian translation. For every tale the edition records where it comes from, its narrators, Calvino's source collection, its ATU tale type and a Propp-based reading of its outcome, animals and places, and an advanced search runs across the corpus.
project.conclusionText: The 2026 version makes the edition usable: a search that finds tales and episodes, the dialect record beside the Italian passage by passage, a map of the tales, catalogue cards comparing the two cycles, an Italian and English interface and a guide to the sources (Calvino, Zorzùt, Pitrè).
project.highlightCaption: The search page: find a tale or an episode by keyword.
project.context: MA Digital Humanities and Digital Knowledge, University of Bologna
project.reworkNote: Digitalian Folktales began as a group project with Nikolai Gorbachev. I reworked it independently in 2026; the version shown here is that rework.

summary.brief: Calvino retold Italy's folktales in standard Italian; the dialect versions he drew on are hard to read against his.
summary.role: Edition design and web development; the 2026 rework on my own.
summary.method: Dialect texts aligned with Italian translations passage by passage; tale types (ATU) and a structural reading recorded for each episode.
summary.outcome: A searchable edition of two tale cycles, Friuli and Sicily: 5 episodes catalogued, 15 aligned passages.

project.shows: Turning scholarly source material into something people can search and read side by side.
